```{r include=FALSE, eval=!"devoirs" %in% (.packages())}
# For stand-alone compilation testing
library(devoirs)
library(mosaicCalc)
```

::: {#exr-titmouse-fight-dish}
Each of these R expressions is intended to be an application of a function to one or more inputs. But each has an error. Correct the errors.

i. `cos(3.1415]` which should give about $-1$.
ii. `sum(3 2 4)` which should give 9.
iii. `prod(6; 7; 8)` which should give 336.
iv. `cumsum(c[5, 9, 3])` which should give `5 14 17`

<!-- Opening answer: tfd-7zr -->
::: {.callout-tip collapse=true `r devoirs:::answer_style()`}
## Answer

i. The square bracket following the input 3.1415 must be a closing parenthesis: should be `cos(3.1415)`.
ii. There are no commas separating the three args: should be `sum(3, 2, 4)`.
iii. Semi-colons are being used to separate the args, but this is invalid. Only commas can be used to separate args. Should be `prod(6, 7, 8)`.
iv. The `cumsum()` function uses parentheses correctly. It takes a single arg which, in this case, is the collection `c(5, 9, 3)`. Like all other functions, `c()` uses parentheses to contain the args.
